report:
The evidence strongly contradicts the assumption of "no" — multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials show that offering HIV self-testing (HIVST) substantially **increases** uptake of HIV testing.

**Key findings:**
- A 2021 systematic review/meta-analysis in *EClinicalMedicine* pooling 13 RCTs found HIVST roughly **doubled** testing uptake in the general population versus standard services (RR 2.09, 95% CI 1.69–2.58, moderate-certainty evidence), with benefits across multiple delivery models (facility-based, community, mail/online distribution) (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/eclinm/article/PIIS2589-5370(21)00271-6/fulltext).
- A companion review focused on men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender people found HIVST increased testing uptake by 1.45 times (RR 1.45, 95% CI 1.20–1.75) and increased testing frequency, while identifying nearly all new HIV cases in some trial settings (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7713313/).
- PLOS ONE (2021) similarly concluded HIVST "has the potential to increase the uptake of HIV testing compared to standard HIV testing services," though optional home-based linkage to care sometimes reduced downstream linkage rates even as testing rates rose (https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0245498).
- The WHO (2023) cites systematic-review evidence that facility-based HIVST achieves uptake "comparable to or higher than" standard testing, supporting policy recommendations to expand self-testing options (https://www.who.int/news/item/22-07-2023-who-recommends-optimizing-hiv-testing-services).

**Caveats:** Most trials provided HIVST kits for free, and effects vary by delivery model and population; some trials showed modest reductions in linkage-to-care after a positive self-test.

**Conclusion:** Contrary to the premise, robust RCT-based evidence indicates offering HIV self-testing does increase testing uptake — often doubling rates versus standard testing — making "no" inconsistent with current evidence.
